---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: AccrualStabilityTriad
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), SUMRANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5)), TREND(RATIO(oancf, sale), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms whose reported income is not inflated by accruals, whose return on assets is stable across years, and whose cash margin is trending up have durable, cash-backed earnings that the market underprices relative to accrual-driven earnings.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The accrual channel identifies how much of income is non-cash, while earnings volatility and the cash-margin trend measure whether the reported level is repeatable. Ranking all three channels jointly rewards only firms where low accruals coincide with genuinely stable, improving cash generation, rather than firms that are merely low-accrual because of one transitory year.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: CashBackedPersistenceGate
EXPRESSION: MUL(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), INDICATOR(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(ib, 0), 5), 4))
HYPOTHESIS: The low-accrual premium is real information only for firms with a persistent record of positive earnings; for firms with intermittent losses, accruals mostly reflect accounting noise and distress dynamics rather than earnings quality.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The indicator gate switches the accrual signal on only when a firm reported positive income in all five prior years, so accrual information is read as a statement about cash backing of durable profits. Gated-out firms receive a neutral zero, which prevents noisy loss-makers from populating the extreme long-short portfolio legs.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: CashSignalToNoise
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), MA(ABS(SUB(ib, oancf)), 3)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: The ratio of smoothed operating cash flow to the average absolute accrual measures how much genuine cash performance a firm produces per unit of accounting adjustment; high values indicate durable cash earnings while low values indicate performance manufactured by accruals.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is an explicit signal-to-noise construction: the numerator is the quality theme's persistent cash-earnings level, the denominator is the accruals theme's magnitude of non-cash distortion, taken in absolute value so that both aggressive and conservative accrual noise are penalized. Three-year averaging removes single-year timing effects, and winsorizing controls the fat tails created by near-zero denominators.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: AccrualNoiseProduct
EXPRESSION: NEG(MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: High accruals are most damaging to future returns when earnings are also unstable, because unstable earnings remove any credible interpretation of accruals as smoothing of a durable profit stream.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The multiplicative rank product is largest only in the doubly-bad corner (high accruals and volatile ROA) and near zero in the doubly-good corner (cash-backed income with stable ROA), so negating it creates a genuine interaction rather than an additive sum of two effects. This design lets the short leg concentrate on firms whose reported income is both non-cash and unrepeatable.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: CashBackingStreakQuality
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), 0), 5), NEG(VOL(RATIO(ni, ceq), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Repeated years of negative accruals (cash flow exceeding income) combined with stable return on equity identify firms with a conservative, habitual accounting regime whose earnings are structurally cash-backed.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Rather than using the accrual level, this counts how many of the last five years were cash-surplus years, converting accruals into a persistence concept that matches the quality theme's stability measure. The interaction distinguishes chronically conservative reporters with steady ROE from firms that happened to post one low-accrual year amid volatile profitability.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: IndustryAdjSloanQuality
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at))), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Within an industry, firms with small balance-sheet working-capital accruals net of depreciation and with stable operating cash flow to assets have the most credible reported performance and earn higher subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Using the classic balance-sheet accrual construction (change in non-cash working capital less depreciation) gives an accrual measure independent of cash-flow-statement reporting conventions, and pairing it with cash-flow stability tests durability directly in cash space. Industry ranking both channels removes sector-level differences in working-capital intensity and cash-flow cyclicality, so the interaction reflects firm-specific accounting quality.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE AccrualStabilityTriad---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is an additive kitchen-sink of three separately published effects (Sloan accruals, earnings volatility, cash-margin trend) with no interaction mechanism, and the nested SUMRANK silently gives the accrual leg 50% weight versus 25% each for the other two, so any result will be hard to attribute and largely a repackaged accrual sort.

---CRITIQUE CashBackedPersistenceGate---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The conditioning logic is coherent and the sign is consistent, but zeroing out gated firms creates a large mass point at exactly zero that will sit mid-distribution and distort quantile breakpoints — a within-eligible-sample rank or a comparison against the ungated accrual baseline is needed for the test to be interpretable.

---CRITIQUE CashSignalToNoise---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The OCF-per-unit-of-absolute-accrual ratio is a genuinely non-standard scale-free construction rather than a relabeled Sloan sort, though ordering will be dominated by near-zero denominators and by sign flips for negative-OCF firms, so winsorization at 1% is unlikely to be sufficient and coverage/stability diagnostics deserve close attention.

---CRITIQUE AccrualNoiseProduct---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The stated mechanism fails the expression: a product of [0,1] ranks is small whenever *either* rank is small, so the long leg pools low-accrual/high-volatility and high-accrual/low-volatility firms with the "doubly-good" corner rather than concentrating on it, and the construction remains monotone in both inputs rather than isolating the claimed interaction.

---CRITIQUE CashBackingStreakQuality---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Recasting accruals as a five-year count of cash-surplus years is a substantively different framing from the standard level sort and pairs sensibly with ROE stability; the main risks are the coarse 0–5 integer ties in one leg of the SUMRANK and negative-book-equity contamination in ni/ceq.

---CRITIQUE IndustryAdjSloanQuality---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The accrual leg is Sloan (1996) essentially verbatim (ΔNWC less depreciation over assets), and industry-adjusting it and adding cash-flow volatility is a well-trodden refinement rather than a new cross-theme mechanism, so this is a rediscovery with cosmetic packaging.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: AccrualPerUnitEarningsNoise
EXPRESSION: NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: A given accrual is far more diagnostic of unsustainable reported performance when the firm's earnings stream is otherwise smooth: scaling accruals by the firm's own ROA volatility converts the accrual into a "how abnormal is this non-cash component relative to this firm's normal earnings noise" statistic, and low values of that statistic identify genuinely cash-backed profits.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: Instead of adding an accrual rank and a volatility rank, quality enters as the scaling metric for the accrual, so the accrual slope is steep for stable-earnings firms (where a large non-cash wedge is a red flag) and flattened for firms whose earnings naturally swing. This removes the earlier additive kitchen-sink weighting problem and yields a single interpretable quantity, winsorized to control small-denominator tails.
REASONING: none

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: WeakestLinkCashQuality
EXPRESSION: MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Credible cash-backed performance requires passing both tests simultaneously; a firm is only as trustworthy as its weaker dimension, so the long leg should contain only firms that are jointly low-accrual and stable-earnings, while any firm failing either test is not rewarded.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: The minimum of the two goodness ranks equals one minus the maximum of the two badness ranks, a genuinely non-additive conjunction: it is high only in the doubly-good corner and cannot be manufactured by an extreme value on one dimension alone, fixing the earlier product-of-badness construction whose long leg pooled mixed cases. The short leg is economically coherent too — firms that are extreme on either aggressive accruals or unstable earnings — so both tails carry the interaction rather than a repackaged single sort.
REASONING: none

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: AccrualRegimeSurpriseWeighted
EXPRESSION: NEG(MUL(ZSCORE(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5)))))
HYPOTHESIS: What matters is not the level of accruals but a break from the firm's own accounting regime: a firm whose current accruals sit at the top of their five-year history while its earnings stream looks unusually stable is smoothing or borrowing from the future, whereas an unusually cash-conservative year in a stable-earnings firm signals understated, durable performance.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The accrual channel is deliberately firm-relative (TS_RANK within own history, cross-sectionally centered by ZSCORE) rather than the Sloan cross-sectional level, so it is not a re-labeled published accrual sort, and the stability rank acts as a multiplicative weight that amplifies or mutes the accrual surprise. Because the accrual term is centered, the weight rescales the slope on both sides — high-stability firms get the strongest long and short exposure, high-volatility firms are shrunk toward neutral.
REASONING: none
